"NASA's Perseverance Rover Successfully Lands on Mars"
The Perseverance Rover, NASA's most advanced spacecraft to date, has successfully touched down on Mars, marking the agency's ninth mission to the Red Planet. The rover, which launched in July 2020, will spend the next two years exploring Jezero Crater in search of signs of ancient microbial life.

"Global COVID-19 Death Toll Tops 4 Million"
The worldwide death toll from the COVID-19 pandemic has surpassed 4 million, according to data from Johns Hopkins University. The milestone comes as countries around the world grapple with new variants of the virus and vaccine distribution efforts continue.

"Biden Administration to Rejoin Paris Agreement"
President Joe Biden has signed an executive order to rejoin the Paris Agreement, the international pact aimed at combating climate change. The U.S. formally left the accord on November 4, 2020, under the Trump administration.

"George Floyd's Family Reaches $27 Million Settlement with Minneapolis"
The family of George Floyd, the African American man whose death in police custody last May sparked global protests, has reached a $27 million settlement with the city of Minneapolis. The agreement comes as the trial of Derek Chauvin, the former police officer charged with Floyd's murder, is set to begin next week.

"China's Lunar New Year Travel Rush Sees Record Numbers"
Despite pleas from authorities to avoid unnecessary travel due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, China is expected to see a record number of trips during the Lunar New Year holiday, which began on February 11. The National Immigration Administration estimates that nearly 2 billion trips will be made during the 40-day period.

"India's Farmers' Protest Enter Fourth Month"
Thousands of Indian farmers have continued their protest against new agricultural reforms, entering the fourth month of demonstrations that have seen clashes with police and calls for the government to repeal the laws. Farmers, mainly from Punjab and Haryana states, have been camping at Delhi's borders since November.

"U.S. Senate Confirms Janet Yellen as First Female Treasury Secretary"
The U.S. Senate has confirmed Janet Yellen as the nation's 78th Treasury secretary, making her the first woman to hold the position. Yellen, a former chair of the Federal Reserve, was sworn in by Vice President Kamala Harris on January 26.

"UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson Announces Roadmap for Lifting Lockdown"
British Prime Minister Boris Johnson has announced a roadmap for gradually easing the country's third national lockdown, with schools set to reopen on March 8 and non-essential shops on April 12, depending on key metrics such as vaccine rollout and infection rates.

"NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Set for First Flight"
NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter is set to make history by becoming the first aircraft to fly on another planet. The small, solar-powered helicopter will attempt its first flight on Mars as early as April, according to a recent update from the space agency.

"U.S. President Biden Meets with Mexican President López Obrador"
U.S. President Joe Biden has met with Mexican President Andrés Manuel López Obrador in Mexico City, marking his first foreign trip since taking office. The leaders discussed a range of issues, including migration, trade, and the COVID-19 pandemic, with Biden emphasizing the importance of the U.S.-Mexico relationship.

"Pfizer and BioNTech's COVID-19 Vaccine Effective Against South African Variant"
Pharmaceutical companies Pfizer and BioNTech have announced that their COVID-19 vaccine is effective against the South African variant of the virus, according to a laboratory study. The variant, known as B.1.351, has raised concerns due to its potential resistance to existing vaccines.

"Alaska's Largest Earthquake in 50 Years Strikes Near Anchorage"
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck near Anchorage, Alaska, on Friday, January 29, causing power outages and road closures but no immediate reports of serious injuries. The quake was the largest to hit the state in nearly 50 years.

"Italy's Prime Minister Mario Draghi Presents New Government"
Italy's new Prime Minister, Mario Draghi, has presented his cabinet to the Italian parliament, marking the start of his five-year term. Draghi, a former head of the European Central Bank, takes over from Giuseppe Conte, who resigned in January amid political turmoil.

"U.S. Jobless Claims Fall to Near Pandemic Low"
The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell to a near-pandemic low last week, according to data from the Labor Department. The latest figures, released on February 11, suggest that the labor market recovery may be gathering steam as the U.S. economy continues to reopen.

"Iraq Holds First Parliamentary Elections Since U.S. Withdrawal"
Iraqis are voting in the country's first parliamentary elections since the withdrawal of U.S. troops in December 2021. The polls, which were originally scheduled for June 2021, were postponed amid political turmoil and the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

"China's Mars Rover Zhurong Begins Science Operations"
China's Zhurong rover has begun its scientific mission on Mars, according to the China National Space Administration. The rover, which landed on the Red Planet in May 2021, will spend the next three Martian months exploring the surface of the Utopia Planitia region.

"French President Emmanuel Macron Tests Positive for COVID-19"
French President Emmanuel Macron has tested positive for COVID-19, his office announced on December 17. The president, who is fully vaccinated, is experiencing mild symptoms and will isolate at home, according to a statement from the Élysée Palace.

"Canadian Truckers Launch Protest Against COVID-19 Vaccine Mandates"
Hundreds of Canadian truckers have launched a cross-country protest against the country's COVID-19 vaccine mandates, with convoys of vehicles blocking streets and causing disruptions in cities across Canada. The "Freedom Convoy" has gained support from some high-profile figures, including former U.S. President Donald Trump.

"Israel's NewGovernment Sworn In, Ending 12-Year Rule of Benjamin Netanyahu"
Israel's new government, led by Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, has been sworn in, ending the 12-year rule of Benjamin Netanyahu. The coalition government, which includes parties from across the political spectrum, was formed after months of political deadlock following four consecutive elections.

"Mozambique's President Nyusi Wins Re-election Amidst Cyclone and Insurgency"
Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi has won re-election with 73% of the vote, according to provisional results from the country's electoral commission. The election was held amidst a humanitarian crisis following a series of devastating cyclones and an ongoing insurgency in the northern province of Cabo Delgado.

"Germany's Parliament Approves Bill to Phase Out Coal Power"
Germany's parliament has approved a bill to phase out coal power by 2038, as the country aims to cut its greenhouse gas emissions to net-zero by 2045. The legislation, which was agreed upon by the country's ruling coalition, will provide financial compensation to regions and companies affected by the phase-out.

"U.S. Launches Airstrikes Against Iranian-Backed Militia in Syria"
The U.S. military has launched airstrikes against Iranian-backed militia targets in eastern Syria, according to a statement from the Pentagon. The strikes, which were carried out on June 27, were in response to recent attacks against American and coalition personnel in Iraq.

"Indonesia's Mount Semeru Erupts, Forcing Thousands to Flee"
Indonesia's Mount Semeru has erupted, spewing ash and lava and forcing thousands of people to flee their homes in the nearby village of Curah Kobokan. The eruption, which began on December 4, has also caused power outages and closed a major highway in East Java province.

"U.N. Warns of 'Catastrophic' Global Food Shortages Due to Climate Change"
The United Nations has warned of "catastrophic" global food shortages due to the impact of climate change on crop yields, according to a report released on February 22. The report, which was compiled by the U.N.'s food agencies, warns that the world is at risk of a food crisis unless urgent action is taken to address the climate crisis.

"Brazil's President Bolsonaro Survives Impeachment Vote in Congress"
Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro has survived an impeachment vote in Congress, with lawmakers rejecting a request to remove him from office over allegations of corruption and abuse of power. The vote, which took place on April 21, came amid growing calls for Bolsonaro's resignation over his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

"Japan's Princess Mako Marries Commoner, Giving Up Royal Status"
Japanese Princess Mako has married her university sweetheart, Kei Komuro, giving up her royal status in accordance with the country's imperial succession laws. The couple, who had been engaged since 2017, married in a low-key ceremony at a Tokyo hotel on October 26.

"UAE and Israel Sign historic Peace Agreement at White House"
The United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Israel have signed a historic peace agreement at the White House, becoming the third Arab country to establish formal diplomatic ties with the Jewish state. The agreement, which was brokered by the Trump administration, follows a similar deal between Israel and Bahrain in September.

"California's Governor Newsom Signs Sweeping Climate Change Legislation"
California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed a series of bills aimed at reducing the state's greenhouse gas emissions to net-zero by 2045. The legislation, which was passed by the state legislature in August, includes measures to phase out fossil fuel-powered vehicles and increase the use of renewable energy.

"South Africa's President Ramaphosa Announces New COVID-19 Restrictions"
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has announced new restrictions to combat the spread of the COVID-19 Omicron variant, which was first detected in the country in late November. The measures, which include a ban on alcohol sales and a curfew, come as the country experiences a surge in cases.

"Italy's Mount Etna Erupts, Spewing Lava and Ash"
Italy's Mount Etna has erupted, sending lava and ash into the air and forcing the closure of the island's main airport. The eruption, which began on February 16, has also caused power outages and closed several roads in the nearby town of Nicolosi.

"India's Supreme Court Strikes Down Colonial-Era Law Criminalizing Gay Sex"
India's Supreme Court has struck down a colonial-era law that criminalized consensual gay sex, in a landmark ruling that was hailed as a victory for LGBTQ+ rights. The decision, which was handed down on September 6, overturns a 2013 ruling that reinstated the law, known as Section 377.

"U.S. and China Agree to Cooperate on Climate Change"
The U.S. and China have agreed to cooperate on climate change, with President Joe Biden and Chinese President Xi Jinping pledging to work together to tackle the global crisis. The agreement, which was reached during a virtual summit on November 15, comes as the two countries seek to repair strained relations.

"Russia Completes Construction of Nord Stream 2 Pipeline"
Russia has completed the construction of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which will transport natural gas from Russia to Germany via the Baltic Sea. The $11 billion project, which has been opposed by the U.S. and several European countries, is set to become operational in the coming months.

"Maldives Elects First Female President"
The Maldives has elected its first female president, as Ibrahim Mohamed Solih secured a comfortable victory in the country's presidential election. Solih, who is from the Maldivian Democratic Party, replaces outgoing president Abdulla Yameen, who was defeated in a surprise result on September 23.

"Turkey's President Erdogan Wins Re-election Amidst Economic Crisis"
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has won re-election, securing a narrow victory in the country's presidential election on June 24. Erdogan, who has been in power since 2003, faced a strong challenge from opposition candidate Muharrem Ince, who conceded defeat but vowed to continue the fight against corruption and authoritarianism.
